rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and design standards solicitation (FCC PELTS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because personal emergency locator transmitters would be relied on for safety of life and property, the Notice proposes technical standards to promote interoperability and design specifications to assure a reasonable level of reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice requests comments on the need for technical standards and design specifications, choice of frequency band (proposed 220-222 MHz), licensing structure (base station license eligibility limited to governmental agencies and private organizations whose primary function is search and rescue; mobile units authorized under base station license), and alternative licensing schemes including shared frequency use and local resolution of channel conflicts. Frequencies 121.500 MHz and 243.000 MHz cannot be used because of existing aviation and maritime emergency systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model performance acceptance standard (CRSTER/MPTER)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be acceptable, the performance of CRSTER at Eastlake and Avon Lake must be as good as, or better than, its performance at Kincaid, Clifty Creek, Muskingum River, and Paradise (USEPA rural model evaluation studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USEPA established minimum performance standards based on existing rural model evaluation studies for four midwestern powerplants; models were evaluated using the same performance measures and scoring schemes so that CRSTER/MPTER final scores for Eastlake and Avon Lake could be compared to the range of scores for those four plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model evaluation data and period requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Model evaluation should use 12 consecutive months during which both SO2 and meteorological data capture are at a maximum. Two meteorological data sets were considered: Cleveland surface/Buffalo upper air NWS data and on-site tower data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eastlake data were collected August 1981–July 1982; Avon Lake November 1980–October 1981. NWS data were used for comparability to 1980 promulgation, but on-site meteorological data were available and used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model accuracy benchmark and treatment of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: CRSTER (and MPTER) were shown to produce the highest and 25 highest concentrations that were generally within 30 percent of the measured values; the 'factor of two' accuracy previously cited was characterized as unimpressive but the site results were substantially better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results falling outside the accuracy range were overpredictions, which increases the margin of safety in emission limitations. Thus overprediction is treated as conservative rather than disqualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lakeshore fumigation evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare Lyons-Cole, CRSTER, and monitored data for hours satisfying lakeshore fumigation criteria (approximately 350 hours for each plant) to assess whether lakeshore fumigation concentrations exceed non-lakeshore predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study found Lyons-Cole overpredicted the highest 1-hour concentrations (conservative), and CRSTER yielded even greater 1-hour concentrations, substantiating USEPA's 1980 finding that lakeshore fumigation concentrations would not be higher than CRSTER/Class A estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical Stack Height Credit requirement (GEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical stack height and merged stack credits must be consistent with USEPA's Stack Height Regulations; creditable Good Engineering Practice (GEP) heights are used in modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where promulgation relied on stack heights inconsistent with current Stack Height Regulations, USEPA may require reexamination; modeling should use creditable GEP heights (example: OEPA modeling for Eastlake used both stacks at creditable GEP heights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Merged stack credit demonstration criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Merged stack credit must be demonstrated following guidance 'Implementation of Stack Height Regulations Exceptions from Restrictions on Credit for Merged Stacks' (October 28, 1985). CEI's demonstration was accepted because it met specific factual criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstration factors cited as justifying merged-stack credit: (1) merging performed in conjunction with installation of new pollution control equipment (ESPs); (2) location of new ESPs prevented tying in ductwork from the new ESPs to existing stacks; (3) taller physical stack height was necessary to avoid a documented building downwash problem (based primarily on fluid modeling studies); (4) existing stacks could be raised only a minimal amount; (5) space constraints precluded building multiple new stacks. USEPA accepted such a demonstration as justifying merged stack credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling practices for repromulgation
rubrics_metrics.description: USEPA intends to rely on CRSTER and MPTER supported by site-specific evaluation studies; where CRSTER-based modeling is not appropriate (e.g., stack height issues), use equivalent models (e.g., MAXT24) with representative multi-year meteorological datasets and consideration of multiple operating loads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Avon Lake—1980 SIP modeling based on CRSTER/MPTER appropriate because assumed stack credits consistent; Eastlake—OEPA ran MAXT24 with five years of representative NWS meteorological data, both stacks at creditable GEP heights, and multiple operating loads; MPTER and MAXT24 considered equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission limits and compliance test/recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific sulfur dioxide emission limitations are proposed for each stack at Eastlake and Avon Lake (e.g., Eastlake Stacks: 5.64 lbs/MMBTU; Avon Lake stacks: listed per stack with 0.32 or 4.65 lbs/MMBTU). The compliance test method is stack gas sampling as specified in 40 CFR 60.46; notification and recordkeeping procedures are those prescribed in 40 CFR 60.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance tests shall be conducted under such conditions as the Administrator shall specify based on representative performance. The owner or operator shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of the performance tests. See 40 CFR 52.1881(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory economic and OMB review certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 5 U.S.C. 605(b), the action must include a certification regarding economic impact on small entities; under Executive Order 12291, the action must be classified as 'Major' or not and submitted to OMB for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document certifies that this SIP revision will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities and that under EO 12291 the action is not 'Major' and has been submitted to OMB.
